solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foretell women’s score for Scots against England

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
rit is a Scots verb meaning to scratch or score a line
E is the abbreviation for England

explanation.surface: A pundit predicts the result of a women's match between Scotland and England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' simply means next to, so the English letter sits beside the Scots word; 'women's score' looks like a match result but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: What is written down beforehand is fixed in advance, so to set it in writing is to predict or decree what will happen.

clue.text: Retired, Henry fills Wednesday being twisted by Spenser

indicators.note: to fill something is to occupy its inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: ret. is the dictionary abbreviation for retired
H is the unit symbol for the henry, of inductance
Wed is the calendar abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pensioner called Henry spends his Wednesdays being tormented by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person's name but is the unit of inductance. WRETHED is Spenser's spelling of wreathed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreathed means coiled or curled round, and Spenser spelt the word this way in The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Desire to make fast husband free

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to hitch is to tie or fasten
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone longs to tie the knot quickly and be rid of a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast' suggests speed, but here fast means secure, as in fastening a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Incline to retain one tax for the Scots

indicators.note: retaining something means keeping hold of it inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: to tend is to have an inclination or lean towards
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A government inclines to keep a single tax in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incline' looks like a verb about attitude but supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a teind is a tithe, the tenth of produce once payable to support the church.

clue.text: In a strange way define the pro as bawdy

indicators.note: doing something in a strange way means doing it out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone oddly describes a professional performer as smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: End-of-the-pier shows were the variety acts staged on British seaside piers, known for saucy innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the cheeky, risqué humour typical of old British seaside variety theatre, hence vulgar or smutty.

clue.text: No good getting into mere story, daughter snarled

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: NG is the common abbreviation for no good
a tale is a story, often a mere invention
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father snaps at his daughter for being caught up in some worthless fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarled' reads as a girl growling, but it is the definition in its sense of knotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarled can mean knotted or twisted together, as with hair or fishing line, which is the same as tangled.

clue.text: Darned time with dictionary

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about wasting time with a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darned' looks like a mild curse but is meant literally, as in mending socks.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe a stocking is to knit or mend its toe, so a sock that has been repaired there has been toed.

clue.text: Fireside rest? What’s more robust?

blocks.note: and adds a further point, like what's more
iron describes something strong, as in an iron constitution

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sit by the fire is the more invigorating option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fireside rest' suggests a nap by the hearth, but rest means a support here.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, or firedog, is a metal stand on the hearth that supports burning logs, so it is a rest for fuel.

clue.text: Ceanothus is gathered early on island and mostly dark blue

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: new crops, like new potatoes, are those gathered early in the season
Jersey is a Channel Island
teal is a dark greenish blue

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a blue-flowered shrub is picked early on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Ceanothus is a shrub with blue flowers, which makes 'dark blue' look like part of the description.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American shrub is a species of Ceanothus whose leaves were brewed as a tea substitute during the American Revolution.

clue.text: Sort of varnish is left beside grand hamper with no top

indicators.note: having no top means the first letter of a down entry is lost

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
on can mean next to, as in a house on the river
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
to foil is to thwart or hamper

explanation.surface: A woodworker describes a varnish, left beside a large wicker basket missing its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb meaning to obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: Long oil describes a varnish containing a high proportion of oil to resin, making it flexible and durable.

clue.text: Blooming Boers’ mess — they raise in relief

indicators.note: blooming is a mild expletive, and something blooming opens out and changes shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the Boers' dining hall, and its diners raising a cheer in relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In relief' suggests gratitude, but relief here is a raised design on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossing produces a raised design on metal, leather or paper, so people who emboss raise patterns in relief.

clue.text: Chas and Dave, eg, in proper limits of talent

indicators.note: here in simply joins the parts in sequence, one following the other
the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and final letters

blocks.note: due means fitting or proper, as in due respect
the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Chas and Dave, the cockney singing pair, show a proper range of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas and Dave were a London pub-rock pair famous for singalong songs. DUETT is an alternative spelling of duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of performers working together can be called a duet, and Chas and Dave were a famous British musical twosome.

clue.text: Insecticides spoiled no trees, no?

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined from its proper state, so the letters are put into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks, worried, whether pesticides have ruined the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and repeated 'no' make it sound like a fretful query about damage to woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotenone is a plant-derived chemical used as a pesticide and fish poison, so rotenones are insect-killing compounds.

clue.text: With penny for it, thrilled being cut off no longer

indicators.note: one thing for another means in place of it, so a letter is swapped

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for an old penny
it points at the letter that leaves, the T sound in the middle of the word
thrilled and excited are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone was delighted to be given a penny for their thoughts, but then the payments stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the definition as obsolete: excide is an old word for cut off or excise.
explanation.definitionFit: Excide is an obsolete verb meaning to excise or remove by cutting, so its past form meant severed.

clue.text: To some extent “swoun” begins to cease to exist in Hardy

definitions.text: to cease to exist in Hardy

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only a portion of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A note on how far an archaic word for fainting starts to mean dying in Thomas Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: Swoun is an old spelling of swoon, which fits a poetic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy used this verb, meaning to not exist or to cease to be, in his poetry.

clue.text: Male anger upended old tax — we’re likely to get loads

indicators.note: to upend is to turn upside down, which in a down entry runs the letters the other way

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
ire is anger
sess is an old spelling of cess, a local tax

explanation.surface: Angry men overturn an ancient tax, and someone expects to come out well ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person plural, so it describes the answer saying who they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who stand to inherit a fortune can say they will probably receive a great deal of money.

clue.text: Joint that’s cooked? Name’s lost for good

indicators.note: something lost in favour of another is replaced by it, so one letter is swapped
cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A cook asks if the roast is done, and someone's reputation is lost forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' serves twice: it is the definition and also the word whose letters are reworked. 'For good' sounds like forever but means in place of good.
explanation.definitionFit: Jigot is a variant spelling of gigot, a leg of mutton or lamb, which is a joint of meat.

clue.text: With the little grey cells leading steer towards eastern mass of stone

definitions.text: With the little grey cells leading

blocks.note: to head for is to steer towards
E is the abbreviation for eastern
M is the symbol for mass
o is a short form of of, as in o'clock
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A Poirot-like detective uses his brain to guide a block of eastern stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass of stone' reads as a single boulder but is three abbreviations. 'Little grey cells' is Hercule Poirot's phrase for the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: With the brain in front means the skull goes first, which is exactly how someone diving or charging forward moves.

clue.text: Measure of book’s power, but with left-hand side in short

indicators.note: but can mean except or without, so one letter goes missing

blocks.note: weight is influence or power, as in carrying weight
W is the abbreviation for with
vo is short for verso, the left-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A critic gauges a book's power, noting a weakness on its left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' marks the abbreviation of verso. 'But with' looks like a connecting phrase but removes one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eightvo is another name for octavo, a book size made by folding each sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: Inter alia, loving and leaving, for instance, turned up on Scots lists

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means flipped to read bottom to top

blocks.note: eg is the abbreviation for for example
in Scots a rund is a list, the selvage or border strip of a cloth

explanation.surface: Someone's loves and departures appear on Scottish registers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' looks like it introduces examples to the definition, but it is wordplay. List here is the fabric sense, an edge strip, not a written list.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving and leaving are verb forms in -ing used as nouns, which grammarians call by this name.

clue.text: It’s uncertain for an undertaker to sniff at old practice

blocks.note: vent is an old verb meaning to sniff or snuff
joins the verb to its object
ure is an obsolete word for use or practice

explanation.surface: A funeral director turns up his nose at a time-honoured custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaker' suggests funerals, but here it is anyone who undertakes a business enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture is a risky enterprise, so for whoever takes it on the outcome is in doubt.

clue.text: Paste is twinkling outside

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it, so a piece is wrapped around

blocks.note: taken as written
a twinkling is a moment, and mo is short for moment

explanation.surface: A fake jewel sparkles on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Paste is fake gemstone glass, which makes 'twinkling' look descriptive, but paste here is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a Japanese fermented soybean paste used to make soups and sauces.

clue.text: This epic Karen could be donkey’s years in trouble

indicators.note: saying the answer plus an extra word could be a jumble means that extra word must first be taken out of the jumble
something in trouble is in disarray, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters removed from the jumble

explanation.surface: A woman named Karen's epic struggle lasts for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the answer plus KAREN together rearrange the letters of 'donkey's years'. Donkey's years is British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Odyssey is an epic poem, and the word also means any long, eventful journey.

clue.text: Touch of driver, for instance

blocks.note: the first two letters of driver, the way Dr shortens doctor
eg is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: The feel of a golf club or a car's handling, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch of driver' reads as a golfer's feel for the club; touch is the definition, meaning a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreg is a small residue or trace, much as a touch of something is a tiny quantity.

clue.text: One under control after being pitted

indicators.note: one thing coming after another is placed behind it, so the later words of the wordplay are written first

blocks.note: ens is a philosophical term for a being or entity
I is the Roman numeral one
led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: Someone is kept in check after being made to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the first two pieces behind the third, so the answer begins with the last word of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is ensiled when stored in a silo or pit, so pitted here means put into a pit for keeping.

clue.text: Hastily erect an entry for celebration

indicators.note: something done hastily is thrown together carelessly, so the letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers rush to put up a gateway for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebration' is a loose definition by example, since an anniversary is usually marked with festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-hundredth anniversary is an occasion that people mark with festivities and commemoration.

clue.text: I must get into swimmer’s form of massage

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: taken as written
a tuna is a fish, and fish are swimmers

explanation.surface: Someone insists on learning a swimmer's style of rubdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests an athlete, but in crosswords it often means a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tui na is a traditional Chinese therapeutic bodywork technique using pushing and grasping on the body.

clue.text: Shakespearean puds, fine when prepared on Sabbath

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by working on it, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
S is an abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Some Elizabethan puddings turn out well when made on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puds' looks like puddings, but pud is also a dialect word for a hand or fist.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used nief or neif for a fist, and a pud is a childish or dialect word for a hand or paw.

clue.text: Assume old-fashioned interest having been cut by pence

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: usury was once the ordinary word for interest on a loan
p is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Someone takes on an outdated attitude after losing interest in a few pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like curiosity but is the money sense, charged on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to take or seize, as in assuming power or a title without the right to it.

clue.text: Ascendant sister, Reformed Episcopal, falls from grace

indicators.note: ascendant means rising, so in a down entry the letters climb from bottom to top

blocks.note: Sr is the abbreviation for sister, as in a nun's title
RE is the abbreviation for Reformed Episcopal

explanation.surface: A senior nun of a reformed church loses her standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The church setting makes 'falls from grace' read as a scandal, while it simply means does wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who falls from grace commits a moral lapse, and to err is to sin or go astray.

clue.text: Inverted stanza in pushing along fixed line

indicators.note: to push along is to leave or move on, so the letters go away
inverted means turned upside down, which runs a down entry the other way

blocks.note: a sixain is a stanza of six lines
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet turns a verse upside down while pressing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a linking preposition, but it is the pair of letters that departs.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a fixed reference line about which something rotates or against which positions are measured.

clue.text: Interest succeeded being held for contracted denial

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside another, so one piece sits within

blocks.note: int. is the abbreviation for interest
s is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A financier's interest is withheld, and the contract is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests a business agreement but means shortened, as with an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortened form of a negative verb phrase is a way of saying something is not so.

clue.text: First sources could be somehow true before Christ and Son

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come in an unknown order

blocks.note: taken as written
Xt is a traditional abbreviation for Christ, from the Greek letter chi
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A scholar muses that the earliest Gospel sources might be accurate about Christ and the Son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before Christ' suggests BC, but before just places one piece ahead of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: An urtext is the original version of a work, from German ur- meaning primal, so earliest sources.

clue.text: Soldier who follows sermon on new life

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: ser. is the dictionary abbreviation for sermon
re means on or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A devoted disciple listens to a sermon about being born again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who follows' and 'sermon' suggest a religious disciple, but the follower is a soldier in the rear rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrefile is a soldier or officer posted in the rear rank of a formation, so walks behind the others.

clue.text: Undoubtedly captured by duff promises

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: sure means certainly or undoubtedly
duff is slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Someone is certainly taken in by worthless pledges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' reads as the British adjective for useless, but it is the noun meaning buttocks, as in get off your duff.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to tell them confidently that something will happen, which is to give a pledge.

clue.text: No more experience tea, almost unknown

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: Assam is a strong Indian tea
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A retired taster will no longer try a mysterious tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No more' marks the definition as obsolete: assay once meant to experience or undergo.
explanation.definitionFit: Assay has an archaic sense of trying or undergoing something, which amounts to having it happen to you.
